Chapter 10: Embodying Antiracism—Everyday Practice and Becoming a Good Ancestor.
We've come full circle now, back to where it all began—thinking about legacy, and the ongoing journey of antiracism.
You know, this work isn’t about finally arriving at some perfect point of “wokeness.” It’s really about living each day in alignment with your values—justice, compassion, and equity—over and over again.
Here’s the guiding idea: antiracism isn’t just a checklist of actions. It’s a way of being.
It means showing up with humility, with courage, and with a mindset that’s always open to learning. It’s about making choices—big and small—that show you’re committed to building a more just world.
So, how do you actually embody antiracism in your everyday life?
First, stay curious. Keep seeking out new perspectives, and don’t be afraid to question your own assumptions.
Next, practice humility. Remember, there’s always more to learn, and it’s okay to be open to correction.
Act with integrity. Let your actions match your values—even when it feels uncomfortable or challenging.
Support others on their journey. Encourage people who are just starting out, share what you’ve learned, and offer resources whenever you can.
And finally, reflect on your legacy. Ask yourself, “How are my choices shaping the world for the people who’ll come after me?”
Think about it like this: maybe you know someone who’s been involved in learning and activism for years. What sets them apart isn’t a sense of being “done”—it’s that they keep listening, adapting, and supporting others. They see themselves as a work in progress, always growing.
The truth is, the journey of antiracism never really ends. Sometimes, the impact you make won’t be obvious, or it might take time to show. But by committing to this practice, day in and day out, you’re helping to build a world where everyone truly has the chance to thrive.
